findings.title: The walk's copyable-vs-prose filter is narrower than the spec's 'every invocation-shaped snippet': a flagless but argumented invocation is skipped, and a bare `gh pr` mention escapes the contract entirely.
findings.recommendation: Resolving the external pass's third CRITICAL, I replaced the family regex with shape extraction plus the filter `snippetArgv(s).some(t => t.startsWith('-'))` — a snippet counts as copyable only if it carries a FLAG. Measured against the three references, that validates 9 snippets where a contract-based prose test validates 15. The six it skips are `gh repo view <owner>/<repo>` in all three references (a flagless but well-formed invocation the delta spec's scenario calls invocation-shaped; it validates ok:true when run) and `gh pr` in all three (which the validator REJECTS as `unknown command "pr" for "gh"` — a real inconsistency in the references that the pre-walk regex also missed, since `gh pr` has no verb). Replace the flag heuristic with a contract-based test: extract by shape (unchanged, family-free), resolve the snippet's command against `contract.commands` by longest leading key, and treat it as PROSE only when the command resolves and NOTHING follows it (`gh pr create` bare, `gh repo view` bare); an unresolved command is always validated, so a mistyped or invented verb still fails. Then either qualify the three `gh pr` mentions in the references (e.g. `the gh pr verbs`) or accept the failure as a real finding — the point is that the sweep decides, not a heuristic.

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Contract-based prose test as described, and reword the three bare `gh pr` prose mentions in the references (they name a command family, not a command, so `the `gh pr` verbs` reads correctly and extracts as prose).

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Contract-based prose test, and leave the `gh pr` mentions as-is so the sweep fails until the references are reworded — a louder signal, at the cost of a red suite until the wording lands in the same walk.

commentary: Scoped as VERIFICATION over the walk's diff rather than a fresh review of the whole change — this session wrote both the code and the walk, and an independent pass has already read the implementation end to end; re-reviewing it here would spend the pass on what the blind reviewer already covered. Every one of the seven external resolutions was re-run rather than read: both value-parse reproductions, both formatting mutations, the explicit-root invocation, the quoted-value pair, and the restored audit-drift reference with its pinned divergence. All hold, and the contract now carries a value type on every one of its 84 flags with none missing. The one finding is a narrowing I introduced while resolving the third CRITICAL: my copyable-vs-prose heuristic is a flag test, and measuring it against a contract-based test shows 9 validated where 15 would be — the same shape of mistake the CRITICAL itself named, a remembered proxy standing in for the contract's own answer. That it took a measurement rather than a reading to see it is the honest lesson: the instrument's coverage needs a number, not a comment claiming completeness. Residual risk unchanged otherwise: whether the help-line parser survives the next gh release, and whether the positional rule is right for verbs the references do not yet use.
